rides.status: built, ungated — 4,879 lines in 10 files plus a 702-line selftest of 267 CHECKS, the largest in the project, wired as pnpm test:game-rides. THE FAIRGROUND TURNS. The cycle runs in the worker at 20 Hz in PARK MINUTES, so capacity / cycleMinutes x 60 is exact at every speed including the soak's 100x — measured, the carousel ran 19 cycles and 456 riders in one park hour against a rated 480. Loading is rate-limited rather than timed, so a quiet ride dispatches early. Breakdowns, downtime, service, queue with a wait estimate, throughput over a rolling park hour, utilisation, satisfaction. Sim tick 0.0008 ms, 51 bytes a frame for three rides. The animation is solved rather than eyeballed: two clocks (the cycle in park minutes, the machine in ride seconds) joined by a drive envelope; a chair swing's chains fly out at an angle solved from tan(theta) = omega^2 (r + L sin theta)/g, taking the seat radius 8.00 m -> 10.53 m at speed; ferris gondolas stay level and lag a degree on the ramps. Content: claims rideRigs, walks packs() AND onPack, switches on no id. Eleven parametric primitives; the showcase registers a runtime pack whose teacups are three levels of nested rotation, and the selftest registers a paratrooper in a third pack and asserts it is not a re-skin. In frame: 6 batches, 74 draw calls, 134 instances, 49,356 triangles = 6.2 % of the 1,200 budget. 0 console errors, 0 hydration warnings. The builder finished — the second of seven to survive to its own report. Six bugs were found by looking or by a check rather than by reading; the one worth repeating is that EVERY PRISM'S TOP CAP HAD ITS NORMAL POINTING DOWN, so every apron, platform and teacup floor rendered pure black, and it survived three rounds because a black slab on the ground reads as a shadow. openIssues: OPEN (guests/rides, the same thinness `shops` has): 124 riders in a whole park day across four machines whose rated throughput is 2,136 an hour. The hook works and the volume does not — same D-006 time compression as the shops queues, where `speed` is metres per PARK minute so a machine 60 m away is a 43-minute walk and scoreVenue divides its worth accordingly. Ride queues are 0 at every sample for the same reason shop queues are.

OPEN (core/sun + guests, and it is the real reason every evening frame is dark): THE GAME'S CLOCK IS SOLAR TIME, SO THE PARK IS OPEN FIVE HOURS AFTER SUNSET. `core/sun.ts` is astronomically correct — 50 deg N, day-of-year offset 91 (1 April), and the elevation crosses zero between 18:00 (+3.30 deg) and 18:30 (-1.49 deg), i.e. sunset at about 18:20. But it treats solar time as clock time. A real park at 50 deg N in April runs on CEST with solar noon near 13:20 local, so its sun sets around 20:20. Meanwhile `guests` opens the park at 09:00 and closes it at 23:00 with an attendance curve that still has 70 % of peak in the park at 19:00 and 36 % at 21:30. So FIVE of the fourteen operating hours are after dark, by design and by nobody's decision. That — not the exposure — is why 18:30 is flat in track's, terrain's and environment's critiques alike: at 18:30 the sun is already BELOW THE HORIZON. The measured exposure pinning is downstream of it: between 17:30 and 18:30 the sun runs 1.326 -> 0.392 -> 0.019 because it is setting, and no metering curve holds dusk under a ceiling through a real sunset. Cheapest honest fix is a timezone offset in `sunAngles` so the clock is a European park's clock rather than a sundial's; +80 to +100 minutes puts sunset at 19:40-20:00 and leaves two or three dark hours instead of five. NOT DONE, and the reason is blast radius rather than doubt: every report and critique in docs/game/ quotes 18:30 numbers, and a builder is working against this tree. It wants its own change with a re-shoot of the affected frames.

OPEN (environment, now measured across a whole day and the cause of a flat frame three other critiques blame): THE AUTO EXPOSURE CARRIES NO INFORMATION FROM 18:00 TO 06:00. Sampled on the environment showcase in clear weather: 05:00 3.6(MAX) · 06:00 3.6(MAX) · 07:00 2.825 · 08:00 2.327 · 10:00 2.012 · 12:00 1.954 · 14:00 2.012 · 16:00 2.327 · 17:30 3.557 · 18:00 3.6(MAX) · 18:30 3.6 · 19:00 3.6 · 19:30 3.6 · 20:00 3.6 · 21:00 3.6 · 22:00 3.6 · 00:00 3.6. Ten of seventeen sampled hours are pinned at EXPOSURE_MAX, and they include the whole golden and blue hour: at 18:00 the sun is still at intensity 0.392 and `night` is 0.02, and the camera is already at its ceiling. Dusk, twilight, full night and midnight are metered identically. The metering only ever moves 1.954 -> 3.557, i.e. 1.82x across the entire day, and it spends that whole range between noon and 17:30. Two things this does NOT say. The ceiling is not obviously wrong — an auto exposure that fully normalises a night scene makes night look like day, which is what EXPOSURE_MAX exists to prevent. And `contrast` sitting at 1.114 at every hour is by design: `mix(1.12, 0.98, env.cloud)` makes it a weather control rather than a time-of-day one. What is wrong is WHERE the curve reaches the ceiling. Between 17:30 and 18:30 the sun collapses 1.326 -> 0.392 -> 0.019, a 70x drop in an hour, so no exponent on the metering curve can hold dusk under the ceiling — the sun's own day curve is the thing to look at first, not the exposure's. Measured with .game-render/_probe/exposure-curve.mjs; NOT fixed, because tuning a day curve one SwiftShader frame at a time is how noon gets broken to fix dusk.

OPEN (trains): the module has NO requests file. Its builder died before writing one, so whatever it wanted from core or from `track` is unrecorded — if something in the module looks like a workaround, it probably is one and nobody wrote down why.

OPEN (demo-park + track, an integration mismatch nobody had measured): THE DEFAULT PARK CANNOT HOLD ANY COASTER THE GAME SHIPS. demo-park reserves a 58 x 48 m plot for `track` (76 x 74 m inside its ring path), and the smallest of the three layouts in TRACK_LAYOUTS measures 53 x 213 m — measured by building each one in node and walking its spline every 2 m: nordwind 979 m / 62 x 392, alte-muehle 900 m / 49 x 397, kleiner-kreisel 610 m / 53 x 213. So /game has no coaster in it, camera's `coaster` preset falls through to plot:coaster and frames empty ground, and `trains` will have nothing to run on in the default park. I tried two compact junior layouts (station, short lift, drop, two turnarounds, a hop, a brake run) to fill the shelf: they measure 58 x 119 m and 39 x 112 m and NEITHER CLOSES — closure error 104.18 m and 51.61 m of position, yaw exact. That is the real cost and it is worth writing down: a circuit has to come back to its own station, and with two 180-degree turnarounds a paperclip ends laterally displaced by twice the radii. The shipped layouts fix that with a 1.5-turn helix and hand-tuned straights (16.8 m, s-bend offset 8.7), which is a tuning problem rather than a parameter choice. Three ways out, in increasing order of honesty: enlarge the plot and re-cut the ring path (demo-park), author a compact CLOSING layout (track, and it wants a solver rather than a person), or accept that the demo park's coaster arrives with `rides` and mark the plot as awaiting it.

OPEN (core, found while measuring the above): `world.finance.cash` ON THE MAIN THREAD IS STALE. The worker's sim moves the money and the store is updated (the HUD is right), but the main thread's copy of the world sits at its boot value forever — measured 250,000,000 while store.get().cash read 250,146,150. Core mirrors entity commands to the main thread and does not mirror finance, so any main-thread module that reads ctx.world.finance.cash to decide something (can the player afford this?) is reading the balance the park opened with. `tools` happens to be safe because it dispatches finance:adjust and reads the store.

OPEN (guests/shops, unchanged by the arrival fix): a queue still does not form. At minute 840 with 928 guests the park has taken 146,150 cents and shops.stats().sim.queue is 0 — about five customers an hour per shop, so an empty counter is the honest steady state rather than a bug. It is the D-006 time-compression tension: `speed` is metres per PARK minute, so a shop 60 m away is a 43-minute walk and scoreVenue divides its worth by 5.8. Until that is resolved, `shops`' frame axis cannot show the thing that makes a shop read as a shop. The module says the same thing about itself in its own weakness list: 534 sales a day across seven shops is six per shop per hour.

OPEN (environment): the overcast cloud layer carries a vertical seam at x = 636-638 — mean column step 0.56-0.61 of 255 against ~0.2 either side, worst single pixel 3.1, i.e. ~1 % contrast, visible only because it is perfectly straight and hundreds of rows long. Absent from clear skies (same scan returns 0.03 with no preferred column).

OPEN (environment or core, found while re-grading paths): at 22:00 every paving mesh's light list reads sun@0.000, sky@0.100, env-moon-light@0.000, scenery-lamp-0@63, scenery-lamp-1@63 — three of the six PBR light slots on the largest surface in the frame go to lights that contribute nothing at that hour, because mesh.lightSources sorts by renderPriority and not by intensity. At medium the lamp pool holds two so the avenue lights anyway; at ultra it holds six against three usable slots, so the disparity widens with the machine. The fix is a renderPriority on the sun and moon lights, or a rig that drops a light at zero intensity.

STILL OPEN (paths, all measured by its critic, none fixed): 50.4 % of the module's triangles are KERB (24,243 of 48,144, 5.05x the surface it edges); no LOD and no spatial split, so those 48,144 are identical across all six camera x time rows and 16.6 % of the overview frame; graph rebuild 11.2-12.9 ms against a 6 ms whole-sim budget; texture generation 3,784.8 ms at `high`; no camber, crossfall or drainage anywhere, two vertices across an eight-metre avenue; two orphan kerb fragments inside a junction cap.

STILL OPEN (environment): twilight crosses through GREEN (132/144/130 at y=230, G above R and B) because Preetham has no ozone term — Chappuis-band absorption is exactly what keeps a real twilight blue instead of passing through green between a warm horizon and a cold zenith. That is a change to the scattering model, not to a constant. And the IBL's ground hemisphere is a knife-edge terminator on the showcase's own mirror ball.

PARTLY CLOSED (track round 3): the timber silhouette LOD is built — the same bents with one tier of bracing instead of up to four, hung off the master mesh with addLODLevel, timber only, swapping at 180 m on medium. STILL OPEN (track): supports are vertical only, so any stretch rolled past 78 degrees gets none — a vertical column would meet the underside edge-on. On the three demo layouts this hits the corkscrew and the top of the loop, which are correctly unsupported in reality too, so nothing floats; a heavily overbanked layout would show gaps.

STILL OPEN (track): a layout is tuned for its train and nothing warns you. The ops shape themselves from a running-speed estimate that reads the train's drag area and rolling resistance, so a car 5 cm narrower builds a different track — two of three layouts closed 5 m worse under a hand-written train spec. A build tool that lets a player swap the train on an existing layout needs a rebuild-and-recheck API that does not exist.

STILL OPEN, measured: the sky's horizon:zenith luminance ratio is about 4.5:1 where a real clear sky is nearer 2:1. That is Preetham's own horizon overshoot (it integrates an infinite air path with no ground and no aerosol scale-height cutoff), not the tone curve — lowering SKY_WHITE to fix it caps the sun's halo at 1.16x the horizon and flattens every sunset. The two candidate remedies are attenuating the near-horizon in-scattering in the model, or a separate curve for the solar lobe. Not attempted; SKY_GAIN stays 0.09.

STILL OPEN: at the overview camera the terrain's far edge is now a hard silhouette against the sky, because the fog that used to hide it was fog. The world simply ends about a kilometre out. That is the terrain module's geometry (world size, or a distant skirt), not the environment module's haze.

STANDING CONSTRAINT, not a defect: no glTF assets are fetched by default, so every module has to look good procedurally and that is graded rather than assumed. Kept in this list because it is the reason several 'why is this a box' findings exist, and because the day somebody adds a kit asset it stops being true.

closedIssues: CLOSED (guests + rides): GUESTS RIDE. `requests/rides.md` §1 asked for the hook and this is it — the `Errand` map guests already used for shops carries a `kind` now ('shop' | 'ride'), and join, place, board, leave and the refusal all route by it, because `RidesSimApi` is deliberately the same five verbs as `ShopsSimApi`. A boarding sets GuestState.RIDING for the ride's own `rideMinutes`, takes the fun relief, and moves happiness by how well the machine's satisfaction matched that archetype's thrill. Measured on the sim side over a full park day at speed 5: 124 riders across four machines (top-spin 82, wave-swinger 17, carousel 22, wheel 3) and 29 HEIGHT REFUSALS — children turned away from the top spin, counted under their own name because a height limit is a fact about the person and a broken machine is an operations problem. GUESTS BUG, found by the shops builder because it had to explain why nobody was buying anything, and confirmed: needs did not rise at ANY speed a player can select. `d.needs` was a Uint8Array written through Math.round, and the per-tick rise is 0.0217 units at speed 1, 0.065 at 3, 0.108 at 5 and 0.217 at 10 — every one rounds to zero. It moves only at 100x, which is the speed the SOAK runs at, so the one test exercising this module ran at the single speed where the bug is invisible. Measured before: 934 of 944 guests idle with no destination after three park hours, mean hunger 24 against urgentAt 170. After widening the column to Float32: mean hunger 115.6 / 116.0 / 115.8 at speeds 1/3/5 after 300 park minutes, identical across speeds, which is what a time-based decay must be. CORE BUG, found by the guests module being photographed: a step control that does nothing while paused. `SimRuntime.tick()` computes dt from clock.speed and skips its whole body at dt <= 0, so the worker's `step` message ran the scheduler over a world that stood still. The screenshot harness runs at speed=0 for repeatability, so every frame of the guests module photographed an empty avenue with 'Guests 0' in the HUD. `runtime.step()` forces one tick at speed 1 now — the only reading of 'one tick' that does not depend on a speed the caller deliberately set to zero — and game-shot.mjs takes --step=N.

guests: `destKind` was declared on GuestStore and allocated nowhere. `allocate` builds the store with `as unknown as GuestStore`, so the compiler was told the column existed and never checked, and grow/zero/serialize/load each listed their byte columns by hand and each missed the same one. Every tick threw. Fixed with a BYTE_FIELDS list the five sites share, a GuestColumn union the type is checked against, and a runtime guard that names an unallocated column.

guests: THREE unsaved accumulators broke save -> resume, and a field-by-field diff of two serialisations found them. The four xoshiro streams were the obvious one; the gate's fractional party debt and the thought scanner's cursor and budget were not. The debt made the first guest to arrive after a save come in at park minute 2006 in the uninterrupted run and 2006.25 in the resumed one — one tick — with the people, their ids and their slots identical. CORRECTION to something this file carried for three rounds: the world's edge fix recorded here as 'more apron, or a distance fade' was half WRONG. The terrain critic measured that the apron already runs to 1,756 m and projects to screen row 188, while the visible step is at row 231 and 900 m out — which is DOME_RADIUS in sky-dome.ts. terrain round 2: extensibility was 4.0, UNDER the 5.0 floor — the first hard-gate failure in this gauntlet. The module touched registry/pack/manifest nowhere at all and its ground catalogue was a switch over indices with 21 colour constants beside it. Ground layers are a manifest now, split the way paths already splits: the PATTERN is an algorithm and stays in code, the colours and relief are data. A pack can retint a built-in in place (by id, so a save's paint indices keep meaning) or add one past the built-ins; a bad recipe is named and skipped. LAYER_COUNT stays 7 and that limit is written down. Pinned by pnpm test:game-registry.

terrain round 2: the shadow proxy was 33.9 % of the whole frame — stride 2 over a 256-cell heightfield is 32,768 triangles rendered once per cascade, 98,304 of the demo park's 290,262 at overview. The critic proved it twice (render list 75.6 % proxy; showcase 141,340 at noon against 43,038 at 18:30, a difference of 98,302). Stride 4 now (3 on ultra): 290,262 -> 216,534 triangles, -73,728, -25.4 %, at an unchanged 145 draw calls, and the frame is indistinguishable.

The `paths` selftest was RED at HEAD in four runs of four while the module's report claimed '25 assertions, all passing'. Nothing ran it — it was not in pnpm test:game. It is `pnpm test:game-paths` now, and the assertion is the PER-QUERY time (0.313 us idle, threshold 2 us) rather than a total that depends on the query count. The old threshold also contradicted the comment above it, which says a loaded machine measures 2x an idle one and the bug it catches was 20x.

paths round 2: exactly ONE lamp reached the paving, at medium, high AND ultra, where the night rig's pool holds two, four and six — the disparity widened the more the machine could afford. mesh.lightSources sorts by renderPriority and a PBR material takes the first maxSimultaneousLights, so with four slots the list was [sun, sky, env-moon-light, lamp-0]: TWO of the four slots on the largest surface in the frame went to lights at intensity 0.000 at 22:00. Six now, matching scenery and track. Zero draw calls, zero triangles, and .game-render/pn/2200-ground.png is the first lit avenue in this project.

paths round 2: a pack carrying `pathStyles` registered, was reported by unclaimedPackKeys(), and changed nothing — registerPathStyle had no caller and the docblock above it said the seam was waiting for core. Core landed that; attachPathStyles closes it and claims both `pathStyles` and `pathMaterials`. Pinned by pnpm test:game-registry: 6 -> 7 styles from a manifest, surface recipe resolving with it, unclaimed keys [].

paths round 2: `path-concrete-slab` was one colour with a grid drawn on it — the exact thing textures.ts opens by saying the per-cell tint prevents. SLAB_M is 1 m and the recipe tiled at 2 m, so the texture held FOUR slabs and repeated every two metres; the albedo read back off the GPU spanned 5.5 of 255, 2.9 %. Four metres and a per-slab tint at 1.15 now. Cobble at 27.4 across 18x18 is the standard it aims at.

scenery round 2: the far foliage imposter drew a RECTANGLE for both species. An earlier critic had called it species-blind; it branches per species and always did — what both branches shared was `addCard`, which draws a quad, so a spruce was a rectangle and a broadleaf a disc of leaves above a bare stick, i.e. a palm. At `overview` 1,289 of the demo park's 1,290 trees are drawn this way, so those few vertices are what the whole mid-ground looks like. `addCard` takes a silhouette `profile` now. Costed by the critic before it was written: widening the LOD break to draw real trees there costs 263,000 triangles and doubles the frame; the profile cost 18,648 (+6.2 %) at unchanged draw calls.

scenery round 2: the triangle allocation was upside down and neither earlier critic saw it. At `ground`, meadow-flowers took 154,848 triangles (35.9 %) of the module's 431,300 and hedge-box 73,364 — 62 % on ground cover against 16 % for all 1,344 trees. At `overview`, hedge-box alone was 29,184 of 79,490 (36.7 %) for 76 one-metre hedges at 340 m, more than every tree in frame. Both now collapse at LOD 2. Net at overview INCLUDING the tree fix: 299,646 -> 290,262 triangles (-9,384) at an unchanged 145 draw calls.

scenery round 2: a pack registered after boot never reached the module — buildCatalog ran once, so registering a pack took registry.items('foliage') 7 -> 9 while the module's catalogue stayed at 26 with every new key null. Nothing subscribed to registry.onPack. A pack from loadPackFromUrl was invisible to the one module whose job is drawing content. Fixed; detaches in dispose.

The two-lamps question is SETTLED and both earlier critics were right: 74 light sites, 72 lamp entities, POOL_BY_PRESET.medium = 2. Both pool lights run at 63.0 at 22:00 and light bench, hedge and grass; no lamp puts a pool on PAVING. Mechanism: all eight path-* materials and terrain-ground carry maxSimultaneousLights = 4 while scenery's carry 6, the scene holds five lights, and lamps sit at renderPriority = -1. Raising the pool is only half the fix; the path materials' light budget is the other half and belongs to `paths`.

CORE BUG, found by the environment critic by DIFFING PNGs rather than reading code, fixed: `?weather=rain` rendered a clear noon. `core/host.ts` wrote `{ weather, forced }` into `world.modules.environment` — a shape it invented — while both halves of the environment module read `slot.kind`, so the flag was accepted, stored and ignored. The rain frame differed from the clear one by 123 of 2,764,800 bytes at `close` and by ZERO at `ground`. The in-game path had always worked, because it goes through the module's command. Core now dispatches `environment:weather` instead of writing another module's state; verified from the URL afterwards at fogDensity 0.000845 and env-rain at 1,385 live particles. Every screenshot of rain, storm or snow taken by anybody on this branch before this was a screenshot of a clear day.

environment round 2: the weather fog was not held to the arithmetic the clear-day fog is. At the rain values it put half a surface's contrast into haze at 447 m — worse than the 660 m the module's own comment condemns as fog on a clear day. The rain term is scaled by `intensity` now, so a shower and a storm differ by more than their particles. Measured half-contrast: clear 1,525 m, overcast 771 m, rain 664 m, storm 605 m.

Three claims in the environment report were measured FALSE by its critic and are corrected in place: '88 % at 340 m' is 96.9 % (88 % is at 689 m, the figure was read off the wrong distance); the shoulder's blue:red pair 2.81/3.70 reproduces as 3.19/4.23 because the sample azimuth was never stated; and 'the park is black, no light rigs exist' was wrong — two scenery-lamp-* lights run at 22:00 and are visibly lit.

CORE BUG, found by the track critic by probing rather than reading, fixed: `packManifestSchema` was a plain `z.object()`, which STRIPS unknown keys — so NO module could ever own a content category of its own. The track module's `trackElements` was deleted before any consumer saw it (`'trackElements' in parsed === false`, and the onPack listener got the stripped copy too), and `registerTrackElementsFromPack` had zero call sites on top of that. The manifest passes unknown keys through now; `registerPackCategory(category, owner)` lets a module claim one (the counterpart to registerKind, one level up) and `unclaimedPackKeys()` reports the rest, so a typo is a named line instead of a silent empty array. Proven end to end and pinned by pnpm test:game-registry: 21 -> 22 elements from a manifest with no TypeScript, and `trackElments` reported by name.

track round 2: bracing is tiered and no bay is skipped. It used to put ONE X per bay whatever its height, and skipped every second timber bay under a comment claiming that is how a real wooden coaster is braced — it is not; a woodie's bents stand 3-4 m apart and every bay between them is braced. Measured like for like at the `close` camera: 772,548 -> 903,924 triangles (+17 %) at an unchanged 90 draw calls.

The account session limit has now killed a fan-out TWICE: 22 agents at xhigh (0 done, 22 errored) and then 3 agents (a demo-park round-2 builder and two critics, all three dead on the same 429). So the ceiling is TOKEN THROUGHPUT, not agent count, and the working assumption is at most one or two subagents at a time — or the integrator does the work in-session, which is how demo-park round 2 was done.

demo-park round 2 (integrator, not a builder): planting now follows the circulation. Trees 893 -> 1,196; within 10 m of a path 6.9 % -> 16.2 %; the 80-120 m band 7.8 -> 46.6 trees/ha, so the bathtub profile the round-1 critic measured is gone. 34 % more trees cost 0 draw calls (145, unchanged) and 1.5 % more triangles, because scenery instances them. 16.2 % rather than 30 % is deliberate and argued in the report: the proxy can be gamed by pulling every setback under 10 m, which would close the canopy over three four-metre loops.

`nextEntityId` kept a process-global `let idCounter` folded in with the world's own `__ids` by a `Math.max`, so the SECOND world built in a process carried on from where the first stopped — the same seed minted `path-1…` once and `path-4…` the next time (measured). Found by the demo-park builder, which builds its park twice to prove it reproduces. Fixed in core: the sequence lives in the world and nowhere else, and `test-game-save-roundtrip` now builds two worlds and compares, which was verified to FAIL with the counter put back.

The sky, the fog and the exposure were all wrong in the same direction and are measured now. Three causes, each verified against a frame: (1) `scene.fogColor` was written as a LINEAR radiance, and Babylon runs `Color3.toLinearSpaceToRef` over it for every PBR material (`BindFogParameters`, `linearSpace` set), so the shader saw 0.034 where 0.295 was written — distant terrain got DARKER with distance instead of paler (sRGB 58/80/42 unfogged against 46/58/44 at 700 m). (2) The DOME painted `SkyState.ground` below the horizon, which is a term the IBL needs and the backdrop must not have: at the overview camera the terrain's far edge sits ~75 px under the true horizon and those 75 px were a dark olive band, sRGB 24/26/18 against the 75 the horizon ring rendered. That band is what several rounds of screenshots read as 'black above the horizon'. It is haze now — the azimuth's own horizon colour carried straight down, which is also the colour the fog takes the terrain to, so the edge dissolves instead of stepping. (3) The clear-day fog density was 0.0008, which with EXP2 plus Babylon's `toLinearSpace(fog)` put half the contrast of a surface 660 m away into the haze: a visibility of ~1.5 km on a day the model calls clear. 0.00035 now.

Auto exposure was a stop under and is 1.85x: EXPOSURE_KEY 0.42 -> 0.78, MIN 0.55 -> 1.0, MAX 2.2 -> 3.6. Those numbers were set against a frame in which the dome rendered black and the fog was four times too dark, so the scene they were metered against was not this scene. Measured at the old values: exposure settled at 1.054 and sunlit grass came out at 0.069 scene-linear, sRGB 80, where a photograph puts it near 120. Pinning exposure by hand and looking: 2.6 washes the grass towards yellow, 2.0 reads as a clear day.

The sky's shoulder ran per channel and therefore desaturated everything it touched — the horizon measured R:G:B 0.80 : 0.94 : 1.00 off the model and rendered grey. It runs on luminance now and scales all three channels by one factor. Measured on the model at noon, blue:red went 1.54 -> 2.81 at dy 0.3 and 2.05 -> 3.70 at dy 0.6, with the levels unchanged.

The camera fallback presets were wrong twice and are fixed twice: `overview` looked 37 degrees down against a 25.8-degree half-FOV, so the horizon was 11.3 degrees OUT of frame and no screenshot of that preset could contain sky; the correction to 23.5 degrees left 36 px of it, so every 'sky' screenshot after that was really a screenshot of the haze band. It is 15.5 degrees now, horizon at 154 px of 720.

SUPERSEDED (budget): 145 draw calls at overview and 237 at ground, 'with six modules unbuilt'. Eleven modules are built now and the current figures are 207 at overview at boot and 323-342 at ground with a park full of guests, i.e. 17-29 % of the 1,200 budget.

CLOSED (harness, not environment — the wet-surface pass was working the whole time): the ground never looked wet because every weather shot in this project was taken at tick ~0. `?weather=` moves the sky, the fog, the exposure and the particles instantly, but `wetness` is an accumulator over PARK MINUTES and the harness runs at speed 0. Measured: 53 s of wall clock in a storm leaves environment.wetness() at 0 and path-concrete-slab at its dry albedoColor 1 / roughness 1; 30 park minutes of --step takes wetness to 0.963 and that material to 0.576 / 0.403 — a 42 % darkening and a 60 % drop in roughness, which is surfaces.ts doing exactly what its docblock says. `.game-render/env-wet-park/0900-ground.png` is the first frame in this project with a wet park in it, and it is the best weather frame the game has. scripts/game-shot.mjs now says so where --weather is parsed. Same shape as the particle problem: the feature worked and the verification loop could not see it.

CLOSED (environment): the rain reads as rain. Three things were wrong and all three were geometry: the emission box was 30 m across so most of the drops paid for never reached the near field; it started 26 m above the camera, which is above a horizontal camera's field of view for most of a drop's life; and the life outlived the fall, so a drop died 18 m below the ground it had landed on. Box 18 m across starting 12 m up, life cut to about the fall time, rate raised into the room that frees, and the streak TEXTURE thinned to a quarter of its width — at the sizes needed to see a drop the old taper drew a cone rather than a line. Measured on the static showcase against the same shot with no particles, pixels above 6 of 255: 0.17 % -> 1.14 % (too fat, cones) -> 0.43 % (thin streaks) -> 0.56 % at the final rate; a storm is denser again. One draw call either way. Frames looked at at each step.

CLOSED (guests): the park no longer takes four hours to make its first sale. Every guest used to be admitted with its needs at a flat 6-42 of 255, so a whole park was identical and about five hours from wanting anything. spawnParty now takes a per-party `preVisit` (0-240 park minutes, uniform) that ages the needs WITHOUT touching arrivedAt/leaveAt — time spent getting to the park, as against time spent inside it, which is what `aged` already meant. Measured from the 09:00 boot at speed 1: takingsToday was 0 at minute 660 and 0 at 720 before; it is 3,950 at 660 and 27,750 at 720 after, i.e. the park trades from its second hour instead of its fifth. pnpm test:game green including the 48-hour soak.

CLOSED (harness): a particle effect could not be photographed at all. Babylon ages particles by updateSpeed x scene.getAnimationRatio(), and that ratio is the real frame delta — 1-3 s under SwiftShader against a 1.15-1.5 s raindrop lifetime, so every drop was born and expired inside one update and every 'rain' frame on this branch was a picture of an overcast day. scripts/game-shot.mjs takes --particles=<seconds per frame> and --particle-frames=<n> now, off by default; 0.1 x 14 is one full lifetime, i.e. the steady state rather than a transient. This matters beyond environment: the whole `effects` module would have been unverifiable the same way.

PARTLY CLOSED (integrator): one of the four passthrough pack categories is now exercised by shipped content and photographed. `neon-lagoon` carries a `cameraPresets` entry (`lagoon`, anchored `park:water | park:centre`), the running game reports 8 presets instead of 7 with `unclaimedPackKeys()` still [], and `node scripts/game-shot.mjs --cam=lagoon` frames the demo park's lake low over the water at 222 draw calls / 0 errors (.game-render/packpreset/1200-lagoon.png, looked at). That is the FIRST frame in this project taken through a content pack's entry in a category a module claimed with registerPackCategory. STILL OPEN for the other three: a groundLayers retint is global by index, so neon-lagoon retinting `grass` would repaint the demo park — the design has no park- or theme-scope; and a pathStyle or a trackElement is only visible once something is built with it, which waits on `tools`. Note the precise claim: the pack SCHEMA's own categories (scenery, shops, rides, trackStyles, foliage, materials) are used heavily by both bundled packs — it is the four later extensions that had no shipped content.

CLOSED (guests round 2): the two models of buying are one. `guests` now calls `shops.find(need, x, z, cash)`, walks to the OFFER's frontage rather than the entity position, `join`s the queue, stands where `place()` says while it waits, `collect`s a receipt or `leave`s as a balk, and `lastRefusal` explains a refusal instead of the guest silently wandering off. Verified by the integrator over a full demo-park day at speed 5, and it agrees to the cent three ways: cash delta 273,550 = guests.spentToday 273,550 = shops.takingsToday 273,550. A/B on the same seed: 292 sales / EUR 2,165.50 / longest line 0 before, 534 / EUR 2,735.50 / longest line 9 after, plus 415 price refusals and 2 balks that used to be silent. fanOut.outcome: FAILED — all 22 builder agents hit the account session limit
fanOut.note: Two agents (terrain, environment) ran for ~70 minutes and produced real, committed work before the limit stopped everything; the other 20 never started. No critic gate ran, so no module has a score. The environment builder was killed mid-sentence while writing its own 'what is weak' section — the integrator filled that section in from measurement and labelled it as such. FIFTH failure: the trains builder died the same way on 2026-09-07, mid-fix, after writing 3,720 lines — it had just diagnosed the addLODLevel-on-thin-instances bug correctly and its last message names the fix. The integrator applied it. Pattern across five: an agent gets 60-90 minutes of real work done and dies during verification or documentation, so the integrator inherits a module that works and has no report. The rides builder FINISHED (2026-09-07), the second agent of seven to reach its own report — and the difference was an instruction in the brief to write the report and requests file EARLY rather than at the end, added after five builders died between working code and finished documentation. Both files were in the tree before most of the code was.
fanOut.lesson: 22 concurrent-capable agents at xhigh effort is more than the account budget allows in one run. A re-run has to be smaller and sequential, not the same fan-out again.
